propositions: A patch-set upload event is delivered at-most-once by Gerrit webhooks, then permanently dropped by reconcile_once() advancing cursor to newest without a low-water mark, causing changes to stall unvoted

The reconciler's unconditional cursor advance past non-voted candidates (error, deferred, review_timeout, reconcile_check_error) silences them from all future windows since ?t1= is a server-side inclusive lower bound
A multi-event reconciler pass with a candidate failing midway loses that candidate forever; the existing test suite does not exercise the since parameter and never saw the defect

Two distinct manual nudges (recheck-review comment and no-op rebase) revive stalled changes by emitting new events with timestamps after the cursor, proving the review was queued on a lost event rather than change state

The reconciler's low-water mark fix must distinguish retryable statuses (error, deferred, reconcile_check_error, review_timeout) from terminal ones (voted, skipped) and bound holdback to RECONCILE_MAX_HOLDBACK_SECONDS to prevent permanent pinning

Observable queue_depth and held_back metrics are required to disambiguate bot-down vs queued vs dropped states, enabling operators and agents to distinguish work-in-progress from silently-lost uploads
